_why_two_claims: AGREEMENT asks whether the engines compute the same thing; RECOVERY asks whether they compute the right thing. Neither implies the other.

truth.source: the fixture's data-generating process: 30% structural zeros, Poisson mean 2 x exp(-0.5 x treated) otherwise

agreement.claim: both engines report the same count-part rate ratio, standard error and interval, count intercept and inflation probability
agreement._note: Observed spread on the committed fixture: up to 2.4e-8 with Python's standard errors from the log-likelihood's numerical Hessian. With statsmodels' own bse the standard error differed from R's by 9.2e-4 (1.2%); an independent Hessian of a written-out log-likelihood matched R, so statsmodels' bse was the outlier. harness/flexible_examples.test.py keeps that comparison as a standing control.

recovery.claim: the rate ratio and both intercepts are close to the fixture's

calibration.rule: about 1.3 times the measured 99th percentile miss, rounded up
calibration.limits: Measured by harness/flexible_examples.test.py over seeds 0 to 99 of this generator.
